annotations.title: Draft an Alert Rule From English

description: Turn a detection idea in plain English into an alert rule draft for one app, checked against that app's data. It reads the app's real event types, attribute keys and routes, then picks the kind: instant (conditions checked on every incoming request, alerts within seconds; one request is enough evidence) or periodic (SQL run on a schedule: counts, thresholds, distinct counts, ratios, sequences, baselines, security events, app log lines). Periodic SQL is run once against the data; instant conditions are replayed over the app's last 2000 requests, so check.matches shows what would alert today (false positives). Nothing is saved: create it with securenow_alert_rule_create, passing the draft fields. To CHANGE an existing rule, pass ruleId and describe the change in text: the draft is the whole rule rewritten (same kind, the rest kept), with `current` showing the rule as it is; apply it with securenow_alert_rule_update (sqlQuery + schedule, or instant {matchMode, conditions, environments}). Waits up to 120 seconds.

applicationKey.description: App key the rule watches; the draft is checked against its data.

confirm.description: Required for write actions. Must be true.

environment.description: Only watch this environment (e.g. production). Omit to watch every environment.

kind.description: Optional: instant or periodic. Omit to let the drafter choose.

reason.description: Short human-readable reason for the write action.

ruleId.description: Optional: an existing custom rule to change; text then describes the change. applicationKey defaults to one the rule watches.

text.description: What the rule should catch, in plain English, e.g. "one IP failing 10 sign-ins in 5 minutes" or "anyone requesting /.env or /.git".

name: securenow_alert_rule_draft
